aesthetic: Papier Gris — a Swiss-editorial system grounded in warm cream fields with umber ink and precise typographic geometry, evoking a high-end architecture monograph printed on uncoated stock
chromaticArc: Slides 1–10 anchor in Cream Paper with Burnt Umber text and hairlines; slides 11–14 shift to Warm Sand grounds for section warmth; slide 15 drops to Warm Ink (first dark divider); slides 16–26 return to Cream Paper with intensifying Burnt Umber accents; slide 27 hits Warm Ink again (second dark divider); slides 28–37 cycle between Cream Paper and Warm Sand as tonal counterpoint; slide 38 closes with a final Warm Ink divider; slides 39–40 resolve back to Cream Paper — three full light-to-dark crossings across the arc.
gridStrategy: Each slide draws from a rotating quartet of zone archetypes — Wide Statement (title col:0 span:58, body col:4 span:48), Sidebar Column (title col:0 span:16, body col:20 span:38), Offset Right (title col:30 span:28, body col:2 span:24), and Centred Editorial (title col:10 span:38, body col:14 span:32) — cycling with deliberate irregularity so no two adjacent slides share the same archetype.

fontStrategy.secondarySlides: Georgia appears on 6 slides (roughly slides 8, 15, 22, 27, 33, 39) — section-opening or reflective text slides where warmth and editorial authority outweigh structural clarity; always in weight 400, tracking 0.

accentStrategy: Thin 1px horizontal lines (type: line) span 20–40 columns to bisect title and body zones on approximately 18 of 40 slides, while small filled bars (col-span 1–2, row-span 2) in Burnt Umber punctuate the left or right gutter on 6 additional slides, giving the deck a rhythm of restrained editorial marks.
